Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Pending Against Kinross Gold Corporation: The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith Highlights Lead Plaintiff Deadline

Suit alleges Kinross Gold Corporation failed to disclose material facts to investors who bought from February 18, 2026 through September 23, 2026; investors may seek lead plaintiff appointment by January 5, 2027

Kinross Gold Corporation ("Kinross" or the "Company") (NYSE: KGC) is the subject of a securities fraud class action lawsuit filed on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired the Company's securities from February 18, 2026 through September 23, 2026, inclusive. The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith today reported the lawsuit, Lin v. Kinross Gold Corporation et al., which was filed on November 6, 2026 in the U.S. District Court Colorado District Court (Case No. 1:26-cv-05910). The deadline for Kinross Gold Corporation investors to file a lead plaintiff motion is January 5, 2027.

Investors with losses on Kinross Gold Corporation securities can contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith about the Kinross Gold Corporation class action to discuss potential claims under the federal securities laws before the January 5, 2027 lead plaintiff deadline.

Important dates in the Kinross Gold Corporation case

  • Complaint filing date: November 6, 2026
  • Court: U.S. District Court Colorado District Court
  • Class period: February 18, 2026 through September 23, 2026, inclusive
  • Deadline for lead plaintiff motions: January 5, 2027

What happened?

On September 23, 2026, Kinross issued an “Operational and Return of Capital Update” that reduced “full-year 2026 and 2027 attributable production to be 2% to 3% below the low end of the previously disclosed guidance, with approximately 1.84 to 1.86 million gold equivalent ounces” per year. The Company attributed the results, in significant part, on lower mining rates and ore recovery challenges at Round Mountain.

On this news, Kinross stock fell $3.20 or 11.59%, to close at $24.42 on September 24, 2026, thereby injuring investors.

Allegations in the Kinross Gold Corporation lawsuit

The Kinross Gold Corporation shareholder lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Kinross Gold Corporation's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) Kinross did not have the necessary resources and/or was otherwise ill equipped to achieve the approximately 2 million gold equivalent ounces ("Au eq. oz.") being projected; and (2) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Kinross Gold Corporation's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Kinross Gold Corporation investors who purchased or otherwise acquired securities during the class period may move the Court by January 5, 2027 to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in this putative class action.

"The lawsuit against Kinross Gold Corporation alleges that, among other things, the Company failed to tell investors that Kinross did not have the necessary resources and/or was otherwise ill equipped to achieve the approximately 2 million gold equivalent ounces ("Au eq. oz.") being projected. Kinross Gold Corporation investors who bought during the class period may be able to pursue their losses through this class action, and the January 5, 2027 lead plaintiff deadline is an important first date," said Howard G. Smith of The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith.

Next steps for Kinross Gold Corporation investors

Kinross Gold Corporation investors who suffered losses may contact The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith to learn about pursuing their claims. For more information, visit the firm's website, email howardsmith@howardsmithlaw.com, or call (215) 638-4847.

To be a member of the Kinross Gold Corporation class, you need not take any action at this time; you may retain counsel of your choice or take no action and remain an absent class member. No class has been certified so far in the Kinross Gold Corporation case.

Common questions from Kinross Gold Corporation investors

Who is eligible? Investors who acquired Kinross Gold Corporation securities from February 18, 2026 through September 23, 2026 and suffered losses may qualify for the class in the Kinross Gold Corporation shareholder lawsuit.

Where is the Kinross Gold Corporation case pending? The Kinross Gold Corporation class action, Lin v. Kinross Gold Corporation et al., is pending in the U.S. District Court Colorado District Court (Case No. 1:26-cv-05910).

Do I have to do anything to be in the Kinross Gold Corporation class? No, Kinross Gold Corporation investors need not take any action at this time and may remain absent class members.

Does it cost anything? The Law Offices of Howard G. Smith works on contingency, meaning Kinross Gold Corporation investors owe no attorneys' fees out of pocket. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses are paid solely from a recovery, if achieved, and require court approval.

The firm prosecutes securities fraud, takeover, and derivative litigation against public companies and their officers, directors, and advisors in federal and state courts nationwide, and has helped clients recover hundreds of millions of dollars in losses. ComEd Recognized as Most Reliable Power Grid in the U.S. With 2026 ReliabilityOne® Awards

Regional reliability and grid flexibility work also recognized with additional awards

ComEd customers are served by the most reliable electric utility in the nation. PA Consulting yesterday presented ComEd with its 2026 ReliabilityOne® National Reliability Award, Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Midwest Region and the Grid Flexibility Awards. ComEd previously won the award in 2023.

"Being named the most reliable electric utility in the country is a credit to the dedication of our ComEd workforce and a demonstration of the value of the targeted investments we have made in our grid over the past decade,” said ComEd President and CEO Gil Quiniones. “Our proposed grid plan charts a path for continuing to deliver nation-leading reliability, while keeping affordability top of mind, even in a future with more extreme weather events and unprecedented growth in power demand. We believe that reliability should not come at the expense of affordability, and we are working hard to keep customer bills as low as possible."

The recognition comes as northern Illinois faces new pressures on its power grid. Families and businesses are using more electricity than ever as homes, vehicles and buildings go electric, and severe storms are becoming more frequent and intense. That’s why ComEd’s Grid Plan which will be decided upon in December, is designed to protect the reliability customers count on today and prepare the grid for the decades ahead.

“Congratulations to ComEd on this national recognition, reinforcing Illinois’ nation-leading position in electric reliability,” said Governor JB Pritzker. “As energy demands continue to grow, we remain focused on strengthening our electric grid, lowering costs for working families and businesses, and building a cleaner, more reliable energy future for all Illinoisans.”

Since ComEd began its smart grid investments in 2012, those upgrades have helped customers avoid nearly 27 million power interruptions and more than $5 billion in outage-related costs. Overall reliability, measured by how long customers are without power, has improved by more than 75 percent compared with the 2007–2011 average. Outages lasting 12 hours or more have fallen 69 percent over the same period. These investments include smart switches that automatically reroute power, stronger poles and wires, modernized substations and better storm preparedness. Together, they have also sped up recovery after severe weather. In 2025, ComEd restored power to half of customers affected by storms within two hours and 98 percent within 24 hours. Had it not been for grid investments, an additional 2.6 million customers would have lost power.

“Reliable energy infrastructure is essential to Illinois’ ability to attract investment, support businesses, and create jobs,” said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. “ComEd is an important partner in that work, and this national recognition underscores the strength of our state’s energy infrastructure."

A recent study by ComEd and Argonne National Laboratories projects that the number of heavy rainfall events, as well as more instances of severe weather, in northern Illinois, defined as those producing more than two inches of precipitation, could nearly double by mid-century. To prepare, ComEd is already bringing more durable technologies to the grid like fibreglass poles and elevated substations, developing management strategies to address severe storms, warmer temperatures, invasive pests and tree health risks that can affect vegetation near power lines and planning for new environmental threats that could affect utility equipment and infrastructure.

Severe weather data helps inform grid investments, including ComEd’s latest multiyear grid plan, filed in January, that builds upon its previous plan to strengthen the grid, continue delivering safe and affordable electric service as well as nation-leading reliability for ComEd’s customers amid the challenges of increasingly extreme weather and rising energy demands. The plan aligns with the state’s clean energy and economic development growth goals reflected in the Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) and the Clean and Reliable Grid Affordability Act (CRGA).

Grid Flexibility Award

ComEd also received the ReliabilityOne® Grid Flexibility Award which is presented to a ReliabilityOne® recipient that demonstrated a dedicated focus on providing its customers and grid users with means to cost effectively use the grid to meet their needs. ComEd demonstrated the ability to interconnect a variety of distribution energy resources as well as the ability to monitor and control their outputs to maintain safe, reliable and resilient power throughout the year. These flexible interconnections have been used to defer system upgrades, helping customers get additional value from existing infrastructure investments and enabling clean energy to be added to the system as cost effectively as possible.

ComEd expects to connect approximately 400 community solar projects by the end of 2026 with a little over 320 interconnected year-to-date. Approximately 500 community solar sites are currently within ComEd’s construction interconnection queue, and more than 500 additional projects are currently in the study phase of interconnection to assess system impact. As of October, approximately 8 gigawatts (GW) of renewable generation are interconnected within the ComEd zone, including 6 GW of utility-scale renewable generation and 2 GW of distributed generation resources. Increasing the supply of solar on the grid is critical to meeting the rising energy demands of Illinois.

All utilities operating electric delivery systems in North America are eligible for consideration for the ReliabilityOne® Award. This year we recognize six leading utilities in their respective regions, which include utilities from the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, Upper Midwest, Southeast, and Pacific Regions. The selection of provisional recipients is based primarily on system reliability statistics that measure the frequency (SAIFI) and duration of customer outages (SAIDI and CAIDI). After provisional recipients are selected, each company undergoes a rigorous certification process which provides an independent review and confirmation of the policies, processes and systems used to collect, analyze and report a company's reliability results. Additional awards are recognized based on analysis of certification findings.

About ComEd

ComEd is a unit of Chicago-based Exelon Corporation (NASDAQ: EXC), a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving more than 10.7 million electricity and natural gas customers. ComEd powers the lives of more than 4 million customers across northern Illinois, or 70 percent of the state's population. For more information visit ComEd.com, and connect with the company on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, and YouTube.

About PA Consulting

PA Consulting believes in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. As strategies, technologies and innovation collide, we create opportunity from complexity. Our diverse teams combine deep expertise, innovative thinking and breakthrough technologies to help clients adapt, transform and achieve enduring results across consumer and manufacturing, defense and security, energy and utilities, financial services, government and public services, health and life sciences, and transport. As a Jacobs company, we combine strategic advisory, design and delivery as a single partner across the full program lifecycle. Together, our global team of approximately 47,000 help clients shape investment decisions, solve complex challenges and deliver lasting outcomes. Discover more at paconsulting.com and connect with PA on LinkedIn and X. PA. Bringing Ingenuity to Life.

PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® Awards are presented to electric utilities providing their customers with the highest levels of reliability in the industry. PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® study is based on standard industry reliability statistics that measure the frequency and duration of electric power outages. As a group, customers of ReliabilityOne® participants on average experienced over 56% fewer sustained outages, and their collective system saw 64% shorter outage durations than the average US investor-owned utility. data.title: We're in our 50s and terrified of a market crash. Should we put $400,000 of our $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have a house worth $450,000. Our combined annual income is $125,000.'

"We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm wondering what your thoughts are on putting our house and other assets into a trust. Could it help reduce taxes or protect our assets from lawsuits, bankruptcy or other unforeseen circumstances? If so, what are the potential downsides or pitfalls?

We have a house worth $450,000 and about $1 million in retirement assets held in various qualified accounts. I'd also be interested in your thoughts on annuities for capital preservation and guaranteed income.

Would it make sense to put $400,000 of our $1 million in qualified retirement accounts into an annuity that would begin paying out at age 65, guaranteeing us $40,000 a year for life, while leaving the remaining $600,000 invested in a brokerage account for capital appreciation?

My spouse and I are 55 and 54, respectively. We're both working and plan to continue until 65. We're terrified of a market crash. We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000.

Curious in the Midwest

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'Nvidia has me spooked ': Should I sell my stocks or buy real estate?

That money you invest in an annuity is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Dear Curious,

I'll outline the advantages of your proposal - and then move on to the cons.

First, the pros of putting your money in an annuity, I presume, are to find a haven for part of your nest egg, albeit at a potentially lower rate than the stock market could provide. If you moved $400,000 from traditional 401(k)s or IRAs into an IRA annuity, the transaction generally would not trigger income taxes or the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, provided the funds are transferred correctly. A direct trustee-to-trustee transfer is typically the simplest approach. If you were selling $400,000 worth of investments in an ordinary brokerage account, however, you could owe capital-gains taxes on any profits realized from the sale.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security, which you presumably plan to take when you reach full retirement age. What you receive depends on the type of annuity: your initial investment, the interest rate or other terms you lock in and, of course, the payment schedule. Payouts can also vary with your age, your sex and whether the product is a joint-life annuity. If you expect to live a long time, a lifetime annuity can protect you from outliving your retirement savings. The trade-off is access: That money is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security.

An annuity is neither a bond nor cash. It works as an insurance contract: you pay an insurance company in exchange for income. An immediate annuity starts paying within a year of purchase, while a deferred annuity starts at a later date. Money in a 401(k) or IRA that is invested in stocks can grow over time and help keep pace with inflation. Annuity income is usually fixed, so it can lose purchasing power as prices rise unless you add an inflation adjustment or rider, but that protection also comes at a price: a lower initial payout. Annuity fees can be as much as 10% of the value of your contract. Surrender charges can be substantial if you withdraw money early.

But I have some questions: I understand why the prospect of $40,000 in guaranteed annual income is tempting. If payments continued for those periods, you would collect $400,000 over 10 years, $800,000 over 20 years and potentially $1.2 million over 30 years. Make sure you read the fine print. Is that $40,000 guaranteed income for one person's lifetime? Or is it for both of your lifetimes? Does the surviving spouse continue to receive the full $40,000-a-year income? Is there a death benefit or return-of-premium provision or rider if one spouse dies? Last but not least, are the $40,000-a-year payments adjusted for inflation?

Don't miss: My wife and I are in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage or invest in a stock market driven by AI?

Investing in the stock market

Third, the pros of leaving the money in the stock market: If you left your $400,000 invested for another 10 years instead of putting it into an annuity, it could grow to approximately $592,000 at an annual return of 4%, $787,000 at 7%, or $864,000 at 8%. These estimates assume annual compounding, with investment earnings reinvested, and exclude taxes, fees and additional contributions. The biggest difference between this scenario and the option of buying an annuity with your $400,000 is that the former is not guaranteed. You are potentially giving up the prospect of a larger return in exchange for security.

An annuity and a trust provide different estate-planning functions. Annuities distribute your assets per the terms of the contract, whereas a trust is designed to manage, protect and distribute your estate during your lifetime and beyond. As this guide on Estate Guru points out, trusts and annuities solve different estate-planning problems: (1) Bypassing probate or buying an annuity isn't an estate plan. (2) A trust can manage your assets if you become incapacitated, provide for minor children or beneficiaries with special needs, address the complications of a blended family and set out the conditions for an inheritance.

Revocable living trusts can benefit people with modest estates, particularly those seeking to avoid probate or plan for incapacity. For families with complicated estates, putting accounts and assets under a single trustee can keep everything running smoothly. It can also help prevent conflicts involving beneficiary designations. Marital trusts matter most in blended families, where each spouse wants to be sure their own children are provided for if the other dies. A special-needs trust can supplement government benefits, while a spendthrift trust can prevent beneficiaries from selling or using their future inheritance as collateral for a loan.

Know what you're buying, and be sure you're doing it for the right reasons.

data.title: Cerrado Gold Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
Highlights:

  • Gold equivalent production of 16,985 Gold Equivalent Ounces (“GEO”) at AISC of $1,546/oz Au during Q3 2026;
  • Adjusted EBITDA of $33.8 million for Q3 2026 and $90.8 million year-to-date
  • Earnings of US$0.04 per basic share outstanding in Q3 2026 and US$0.16 per share Year to Date, excluding one-time adjustments
  • Strong cash position of $33.9 million at quarter end includes $8 million cash paid to Sprott Stream during the quarter
  • Full year production expected at the upper end of 2026 annual production guidance of 50,000 to 60,000 GEO
  • Preliminary Economic Assessment for MDN targeted for the end of Q1 2027
  • Continued progress at both the Lagoa Salgada and Mont Sorcier projects
  • Subsequent to quarter-end, the Company acquired Minera Tritón Argentina S.A., owner of the past-producing Manantial Espejo mine in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina (see press release dated November 13, 2026)
  • Management to host conference call on November 23, 2026, at 11:00 AM EDT

TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cerrado Gold Inc. [TSX.V:CERT][OTCQX:CRDOF; FRA:BAI0] (“Cerrado” or the “Company”) announces its operational and financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3/26”), including its Minera Don Nicolas (“MDN”) gold mine in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, its Lagoa Salgada Polymetallic Project in Portugal, and its Mont Sorcier High Purity direct reduced iron (“DRI”) Iron Project in Quebec. All amounts are in US dollars unless otherwise noted.

Production results for MDN were previously released on October 19, 2026. The Company’s financial results are reported and available on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.com) and the Company’s website (www.cerradogold.com).

Q3/26 MDN Operating Highlights:

  • Q3 production of 16,685 GEO, up 21% from 13,832 GEO in Q3 2025. Year-to-date production of 44,942 GEO, up 23% from 36,433 GEO in the comparable 2025 period
  • AISC of $1,546/oz per GEO during Q3 2026
  • Heap leach production remained steady at 9,649 GEO in the quarter, similar to Q2 2026
  • CIL production increased to 7,036 GEO in Q3, primarily driven by the selective routing of high-grade Calandrias feed to the Martinetas mill rather than the heap leach pad
  • Preliminary Economic Assessment for MDN incorporating results of the ongoing exploration program and recent property acquisitions, to evaluate potential resource growth, mine life extension and increased production levels targeted for the end of Q1 2027

Mark Brennan, CEO and Chairman, commented, "Third quarter results continued to benefit from significant operational improvements, cost reduction programs and the repurchase of the MDN stream. MDN continues to generate strong cash flows and stable production. We expect this to continue, given the previous operational upgrades and our unhedged gold position. We expect the new PEA, to be completed by the end of Q1 2027, to show the potential for further growth and mine life extension at MDN. Further, the recent acquisition of Manantial Espejo in Argentina positions the Company for production growth exiting 2027. We expect this growth to be supported by cash flows generated from operations and our strong cash position.”

Operations in Q3 2026 delivered continued strong production, reflecting improvements completed over the past year. Heap leach operations continued to benefit from the resolution of prior irrigation issues and improvements to the crushing circuit. The new crushing plant is undergoing commissioning and is expected to support increased feed delivery to the pad. The new tailings dam is now operational and is expected to provide approximately five years of capacity at planned operating rates. The new heap leach pad is expected to be completed by late Q1 2027 and to provide 12 million tonnes of additional capacity.

Higher gold prices have enabled MDN to incorporate additional low-grade material into the heap leach feed, improving resource utilization. At the same time, selected high-grade Calandrias material originally earmarked for the pad has been redirected to the Martinetas CIL mill to achieve higher recoveries. This material therefore contributes to CIL production rather than heap leach production, and performance should be considered across the combined operation. This strategy is planned to be used going forward to maximize gold production and overall margins.

Selected high-grade material from Calandrias, generally above 2.5 g/t gold, was transported to Martinetas for carbon-in-leach (“CIL”) processing rather than placing it on the heap leach pad. Routing decisions are supported by laboratory bottle-roll testing on milled samples, with selected material achieving gold recoveries of up to 95%, compared with approximately 60% expected through heap leaching as outlined in the current technical report entitled “Technical Report on the Preliminary Economic Assessment of the Minera Don Nicolas Gold Project, Santa Cruz, Argentina ” with an effective date of September 19, 2024. These are laboratory results for selected material, rather than overall plant recovery, and may not be representative of recoveries achieved in production. Management believes the additional gold recovered provides an economic benefit, even after accounting for higher processing and transportation costs.

The focus on underground development continued during the quarter, with higher amounts of fresh feed becoming available towards quarter-end. Additional underground mineralized material is expected in Q4 2026, supporting increased production in the second half of 2026 compared to the first half. Underground operations continue to alternate between development and feed extraction as the workings follow the mineralized zone deeper beneath the Paloma pit.

As the Company continues to advance its exploration program at MDN and drill test the recently acquired Falcon and Calandrias II properties for potential mineral resources, the Company continues with its plans to complete a new, third-party, independent Preliminary Economic Assessment (“PEA”) by the end of Q1 2027. The PEA is expected to incorporate an updated mineral resource estimate, including mineral resources amenable to both heap leach production and production via the CIL plant. The objective of the new PEA is to evaluate potential growth in MDN’s mineral resource base, the potential extension in mine life, and the potential to increase production rates. Over the last two years, MDN has invested heavily in creating twin production streams via both the CIL and heap leach production routes. The CIL and heap leach facilities provide flexibility to process both high- and low-grade material through the most suitable route, based on metallurgical performance and economics. Combined with surface and underground mining capability, this allows MDN to draw on multiple feed sources and optimize the overall production mix.

Exploration work continued throughout the quarter across the existing property and in the recently acquired Falcon area. Sampling and mapping have been initiated, and diamond drilling has commenced in these new areas. Given the extent of existing drilling and the level of work completed at Falcon and other areas to date, the planned drill program is intended to test the potential to add mineral resources to support the expansion of heap leach operations. The Company expects to complete the drill program and associated testing before year-end so that the results can be included in the PEA. Exploration drilling will continue thereafter. Further regional consolidation remains a key corporate strategy objective.

At Lagoa Salgada, the Company continues to advance the Optimized Feasibility Study (“OFS”) and the RECAPE (environmental compliance report on the execution project) engineering phase to bring the project to a construction decision in the shortest timeframe possible. The Company also plans to submit a new Environmental Impact Assessment once the RECAPE phase is completed, which the Portuguese environmental authorities will have up to 120 days to review. As such, the commencement of construction could occur in late 2027, subject to the permits being issued and financing being secured.

In Canada, at the Mont Sorcier high grade iron project operated by Cerrado’s wholly owned subsidiary, Voyager Metals Inc., work continued to advance the project with several workstreams ongoing related to permitting, social license, and various trade-off studies for the feasibility study (“FS”). As the FS progressed, the Company identified several opportunities to further optimize project economics and reduce both capital and operating costs, despite ongoing industry-wide inflation. Several trade-off studies are expected to be completed to evaluate and capture these improvements. As such, the FS is now targeted for completion in H1 2027 (see press release dated July 15, 2026).

The most significant opportunity to enhance the project is to convert a modest amount of currently inferred mineral resources to measured mineral resources within a defined area to the east of the current planned pit. The material in this region is expected to be shallower and should reduce stripping and tailings management costs over the life of mine. As a result, the Company undertook an immaterial, targeted definition drill program in Q3 2026 with the objective of upgrading inferred mineral resources to a higher-confidence category for incorporation into the optimized mine plan. Additional trade-off studies will also be undertaken on product quality and an overall review of OPEX and CAPEX estimates in light of ongoing inflation. Work on the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ("ESIA") remains ongoing and remains targeted for late Q2 2027; however, there is some risk of this timeline slipping depending on the timing of completion of the FS. We note that recent comments by policymakers indicate a desire to accelerate the permitting process; however, no clear timeline for how this will impact Mont Sorcier is available at this time.

The Mont Sorcier project is currently being designed as an 8 million tonnes per annum (“Mtpa”) concentrate operation, compared with 5 Mtpa in the previous Mont Sorcier preliminary economic assessment, to reflect strong demand for high-grade 67% iron concentrates with low silica and alumina suitable for the DRI or pellet feed markets, the fastest growing segments of the iron ore market for which premium prices are expected. Development is expected to occur in two phases, with Phase 1 producing 4 Mtpa and a second 4 Mtpa expansion targeted approximately three years after start-up. That said, based on the trade-off studies and market pricing, this development scenario could change.

Corporate Activities

On July 17, 2026, the Company completed the repurchase of all of the outstanding streaming assets and related security held over the Company's producing Minera Don Nicolas mine in Argentina and its Lagoa Salgada project in Portugal from Sprott Private Resource Streaming and Royalty (B) Corp. ("Sprott Streaming") and Sprott Private Resource Streaming and Royalty (Collector) LP ("Sprott Collector", and collectively, the "Sellers"), pursuant to an acquisition agreement dated July 17, 2026 among the Company and the Sellers (the "Acquisition Agreement"), for aggregate consideration of approximately US$31.34 million (the "Stream Repurchase Transaction").

The aggregate purchase price for the Stream Repurchase Transaction was approximately US$31.34 million satisfied through:

The Deferred Payment Notes are secured by a general security agreement over the assets of the Company. The October 2026 Note was repaid in full on October 6, 2026.

The Company announced completion of the Stream Repurchase Transaction by news release dated July 20, 2026.

Acquisition of Minera Tritón Argentina S.A.

The Company also entered into a share purchase agreement dated November 12, 2026 (the “Agreement”) with Pan American Silver Corp. (“Pan American”) and Aquiline Resources Inc. to acquire all of the issued and outstanding shares of Minera Tritón Argentina S.A. (“MTA”), the owner of the past-producing Manantial Espejo mine and the related mining concessions located in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina (the “MTA Property”) (the “MTA Transaction”). The MTA Transaction closed November 12, 2026.

MTA’s operations consist of the Manantial Espejo mine, situated in Santa Cruz Province, approximately 160 kilometers west of Puerto San Julián on Route 25 and 50 kilometers west of Gobernador Gregores, in southern Argentina (Patagonia). Cerrado plans to implement a phased redevelopment program to dewater historical underground workings while refurbishing surface infrastructure. In parallel, an exploration program has been defined to test for mineral resources in areas not previously mined, with the objective of supporting a potential restart and extended mine life. Subject to the results of this work, the Company believes the MTA Property has the potential to contribute to increased production levels exiting 2027.

data.title: ROHM Develops TP-PFC Controller IC for GaN High-Frequency Switching
data.description:
Santa Clara, CA and Kyoto, Japan, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ROHM Semiconductor today announced it has developed the BM85060FV, a totem-pole power factor correction (TP-PFC) controller IC for high-efficiency, compact AC-DC power supplies. A key feature is its ability to operate in the MHz band, supporting high-frequency switching with GaN HEMTs.

As consumer electronics and industrial equipment become more sophisticated, they require more power while also demanding smaller size and higher efficiency. Stricter energy regulations further drive the need for both improved operating efficiency and lower no-load power consumption. GaN HEMTs are gaining adoption due to their high-frequency switching performance.

Additionally, when paired with a bridgeless TP-PFC controller such as BM85060FV, system designers can significantly reduce power loss and solution footprint, enabling compact, high-efficiency power supplies. However, conventional MCU-based TP-PFC control has posed challenges in terms of power consumption, circuit size, cost, and achieving high-frequency switching with GaN HEMTs.

This new product enables a system-level efficiency of 99% in 300 to 500 W-class AC-DC power supplies. The high switching frequency allows for the miniaturization of peripheral components, resulting in a smaller solution footprint.

No-load current consumption of 150 μA - a 70%* reduction compared to standard products - makes it easier to reduce system standby power consumption and contributes to the development of power supply systems that meet the energy-saving requirements of DOE Level 7 and CoC Tier 2.

Furthermore, the device incorporates various protection functions required for AC-DC power supplies, including a lightning surge protection circuit, which helps reduce the design burden and improve system reliability.

Sales of the new product began in November 2026. Online sales have also started, and it is available for purchase through online distributors such as DigiKey, Mouser and Farnell. Additionally, a 330W output TP-PFC evaluation board featuring the “BM85060FV” is available to support the development of high-efficiency AC-DC power supplies utilizing GaN HEMTs.

ROHM will continue to contribute to the further miniaturization and power efficiency of electronic devices by providing power solutions that combine power semiconductors - including GaN HEMTs - with analog ICs designed to maximize their performance.

Application Examples
• AC adapters
• Consumer electronics such as projectors
• Compact industrial equipment
Ideal for high-efficiency, compact 300–500 W-class AC-DC power supplies.

TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Osisko Gold Group Inc. (NYSE: OGG, TSXV: OGG) ("Osisko Gold" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Wen Hou to the board of directors of the Company (the "Board"), effective immediately (the "Appointment"). Mr. Hou has been appointed to the Board as the nominee of Double Zero Capital, LP ("Double Zero"), the Company's largest shareholder with approximately 15.4% of the issued and outstanding common shares (on a non-diluted basis), pursuant to the investor rights agreement between the Company and Double Zero dated effective August 15, 2025 (the "Investor Rights Agreement").

"On behalf of the Board, we are pleased to welcome Wen as an independent director," commented Sean Roosen, Chairman and CEO. "Double Zero has been a strong supporter of the Company over the past year and a half, anchoring several key financings with cornerstone investments that were instrumental in advancing the Cariboo Gold Project toward a final investment decision and securing the required construction funding. Wen brings a unique capital markets perspective informed by more than a decade of investing experience across equities, commodities, futures, and digital technology coupled with a background in engineering. His appointment further aligns the Board with shareholders as we continue to execute on the construction of the Cariboo Gold Project toward first gold in 2029."

Mr. Hou is an investor and fund manager with more than a decade of experience investing across equities, commodities and futures. He is the founder and Chief Investment Officer of Coincident Capital, a hedge fund established in 2019 that focuses on discretionary trend-following strategies in commodities and digital asset markets. He also serves as a fund manager of Brand Name GP LLC, Double Zero's general partner. Mr. Hou leads the Hou Family Office, where he oversees its real estate investments and private equity arm, which invests in precious metals, commodity funds and trading, and early-stage artificial intelligence software companies. Prior to his investment career, Mr. Hou worked as an integrated circuit design engineer at Intel Corporation. Mr. Hou holds a Master of Science in Electrical Engineering from the Henry Samueli School of Engineering at the University of California, Irvine.

data.title: A Night for the History Books: IAS Celebrates 42 Years with a Monumental Victory for Religious Freedom
data.description:
A Night for the History Books: IAS Celebrates 42 Years with a Monumental Victory for Religious Freedom

A Night for the History Books: IAS Celebrates 42 Years with a Monumental Victory for Religious Freedom

PR Newswire

EAST GRINSTEAD, England, Nov. 19, 2026

Thousands gather at Saint Hill for the International Association of Scientologists' 42nd Anniversary, celebrating a historic victory in Germany, worldwide humanitarian achievements and a new milestone in the IAS's global reach.

EAST GRINSTEAD, England, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As autumn evening descended over the rolling hills of West Sussex, headlights wound along the country roads toward Saint Hill, the historic home of Scientology Founder L. Ron Hubbard.

 IAS marks 42 years at Saint Hill with the end of Germany's 29-year intelligence operation against Scientology

The stirring sound of Highland bagpipes welcomed thousands of Scientologists and guests arriving from six continents for the 42nd Anniversary Celebration of the International Association of Scientologists (IAS).

Flags of nations from across the globe lined the approach to Saint Hill Manor, as elegantly attired guests made their way along the red carpet toward the Grand Marquee. Inside, the excitement of reunions and anticipation of the evening ahead filled the air.

Then, as the lights fell, thousands rose to their feet in a thunderous standing ovation to welcome Mr. David Miscavige, ecclesiastical leader of the Scientology religion.

"There are those who watch history unfold. There are those who wonder what tomorrow will bring. And there are those who determine what tomorrow will be," Mr. Miscavige began. "And if ever there were a gathering of that third kind—well, ladies and gentlemen, you have come to the right place."

It was a fitting declaration for an organization born at this very place in 1984, when Scientologists gathered at Saint Hill and pledged to unite, advance, support and protect their religion and fellow Scientologists throughout the world.

At the time, Scientology had a presence in just 39 nations.

Now, 42 years later, Mr. Miscavige announced a milestone that spoke to the worldwide fulfillment of that original pledge.

The IAS now has members in every nation on Earth.

GERMANY: A HISTORIC TRIUMPH FOR RELIGIOUS FREEDOM

Then came the announcement that would make this 42nd Anniversary a night for the history books.

For nearly three decades, Scientologists in Germany had endured a relentless campaign of government-sponsored religious persecution in the heart of a modern Western democracy.

In a nation whose history bears some of the darkest chapters of religious persecution, Germany had once again singled out a minority religion for systematic discrimination. Government-appointed "Sect Commissioners" fueled an atmosphere of intolerance, while Scientologists faced exclusion from employment, political participation and ordinary business opportunities.

And overarching it all was a nationwide domestic intelligence operation conducted by Germany's euphemistically named Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

But German Scientologists did not stand alone. Nor did they stand silent.

Joined by IAS members from around the world, they marched by the thousands through Berlin to the Brandenburg Gate, demanding religious freedom. An international campaign exposed Germany's discriminatory practices before the world, drawing condemnation and scrutiny from governments and human rights organizations. The United States repeatedly documented the discrimination in its annual human rights and religious freedom reports.

And all the while, year after year, Scientologists fought for their rights in German courts, securing no less than 56 landmark legal victories.

Yet the government's intelligence operation continued.

Until May 14, 2026.

After 29 years of allegations, investigations and relentless government scrutiny, Germany's federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution finally threw in the towel.

Its nationwide domestic intelligence operation against Scientology was over.

The announcement brought the Grand Marquee to its feet, marking a monumental victory for religious freedom and a defining moment in the history of the IAS.

But the evening held another extraordinary revelation.

For while Germany had quietly closed its intelligence operation, the files behind that campaign were about to be opened to the world.

Mr. Miscavige unveiled The Brainwashing of a Nation: Germany's Scientology File, a 500-page exposé by Peter Schulte, a former Commissioner for Religious and Worldview Affairs who had spent 12 years within the very system he now investigates.

Drawing upon Germany's own police records, intelligence files and internal government memoranda, Schulte's work lays bare the stark contradictions between the accusations leveled against Scientology and what government officials acknowledged behind closed doors—including records describing the campaign as politically motivated and Scientology as no threat.

After three decades of accusations, the German people would now have the opportunity to examine the government's own files for themselves.

And for the thousands celebrating at Saint Hill, it was a triumph worthy of the IAS pledge: to unite, advance, support and protect the Scientology religion and Scientologists in every part of the world.

A WORLDWIDE MOVEMENT FOR HUMANITY

From that historic triumph, the celebration swept across continents, illuminating the far-reaching accomplishments of IAS-sponsored humanitarian initiatives.

The Citizens Commission on Human Rights (CCHR) took center stage with three landmark achievements in its campaign against psychiatric abuse:

  • South Africa: Nearly 50 years after CCHR exposed the brutal psychiatric abuse of Black South Africans under apartheid, only to have the government outlaw such reporting, CCHR activist Luce-Lynn Fondling helped protect more than 50,000 children from psychiatric drugging across 45 schools. She then carried evidence of abuse against the elderly into parliament, helping advance new legal protections. And in a nation that once outlawed reporting psychiatric abuse, CCHR has now secured a parliamentary office expressly established to receive those very complaints.

  • Taiwan: Confronting a psychiatric system where 94 percent of involuntary commitments received routine approval, CCHR brought its evidence of patient rights violations before Taiwan's International Human Rights Review. The breakthrough: an international human rights committee called for independent oversight and unannounced inspections of psychiatric institutions, bringing unprecedented international scrutiny to abuses behind closed doors.

  • Ireland: After decades of CCHR exposés, documentaries, petitions and demands to end psychiatric coercion, Ireland enacted a sweeping new Mental Health Act. Among its landmark protections: tighter safeguards against involuntary detention and psychiatric restraint, and an outright prohibition on electroconvulsive therapy for anyone under 18, with or without consent.

But as Mr. Miscavige next declared, "There is more to changing the course of history than bringing injustice to an end. There is also the work of building a better world in its place."

That mission unfolded across the globe, through IAS-sponsored humanitarian campaigns bringing solutions to communities on every continent.

  • Foundation for a Drug-Free World: In a year of three of the world's greatest sporting spectacles, The Truth About Drugs was everywhere. At Super Bowl LX in California, volunteers distributed more than one million drug-education booklets. At Italy's Winter Olympics, another two million. Then came the biggest of them all: the FIFA World Cup, spanning three nations and 16 host cities, with more than four million booklets distributed—the largest single outreach in Drug-Free World history. By year's end, the campaign had reached 162 nations, with nearly 17 million booklets placed in public hands.

But beyond the sheer scale of worldwide distribution, Michoacán, Mexico, provided a model example of what happens when The Truth About Drugs is placed in the hands of those who can put it to work. In a state long ravaged by drug cartels, former police officer and national police instructor Edgar Castillo used the campaign's Educator's Kit to train more than 1,000 police officers and cadets before joining forces with a state congresswoman to launch PREVEMICH—Prevention for Michoacán. The result: a statewide network of police, teachers and youth leaders carrying drug education into schools and communities across all 113 municipalities, turning a center of drug production into a force for drug prevention.

  • United for Human Rights: In Timor-Leste, a nation born from decades of occupation and violence, Youth for Human Rights Ambassador Gabriel Amaral brought the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to a generation growing up in the shadow of conflict. Beginning with rival schools torn by youth violence, his campaign expanded to more than 800 schools and nearly 60,000 people nationwide—transforming the legacy of conflict into a movement for human rights that earned recognition from the nation's President and Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Dr. José Ramos-Horta.

  • Scientology Volunteer Ministers: Mother Nature showed little mercy in 2026. But wherever disaster struck, the familiar yellow shirts of Scientology Volunteer Ministers were there. From earthquakes and typhoons to devastating floods and landslides, they answered 16 disasters across 14 nations, delivering more than 140,000 hours of help to over 600,000 people. It was the latest chapter in a quarter-century of unwavering service: since 9/11, Volunteer Ministers have deployed to virtually every major disaster on Earth, reaching 465 disaster sites and providing 19 million hours of relief.

It was a sweeping testament to the IAS mission: bringing practical solutions to communities, protecting human rights and delivering help wherever it was needed.

HONORING THE INDIVIDUALS WHO CHANGE THE WORLD

The Anniversary Celebration reached another pinnacle with the presentation of the IAS Freedom Medals, honoring three exceptional Scientologists whose decades of courage, dedication and achievement have left an enduring mark on nations and countless lives.

Isabel Ayuso of Spain was honored for nearly four decades championing religious freedom. From the landmark legal battles that secured Scientology's vindication and official religious recognition in Spain, she went on to establish new avenues for defending freedom of belief and advancing humanitarian causes. Through Fundación Mejora, she secured official public benefit status, opening the way for humanitarian campaigns that have reached more than 11 million people across Spain. And with the foundation gaining special consultative status at the United Nations, she carried her lifelong cause from the courtrooms of Madrid to the world stage.

Joava Good of the United States received the Freedom Medal for 25 years on the front lines of disaster relief. Her mission began at Ground Zero following September 11, 2001, and grew into a lifetime of answering humanity's most urgent calls for help. From hurricanes and earthquakes to wildfires and floods, she has led or supported 56 disaster-relief operations, forged more than 140 partnerships and risen to President of the Mountain West Region of Voluntary Organizations Active in Disaster. With more than 30 awards and recognitions for her service, she stands among the most accomplished Scientology Volunteer Ministers in history.

Naseema Qureshi of Sri Lanka was recognized for a remarkable campaign to bring unity to a nation long scarred by civil war and religious division. Through The Way to Happiness, L. Ron Hubbard's nonreligious moral code, she brought Buddhist, Hindu, Muslim and Christian leaders together behind a common pledge for peace and tolerance. From there, she carried the campaign into communities and institutions nationwide, securing the endorsement of Sri Lanka's highest Buddhist authority and authorization for The Way to Happiness in more than 10,000 schools. Her work has helped transform a message of mutual respect into a nationwide movement for brotherhood.

As the three recipients were honored, the Grand Marquee resounded with applause, celebrating lives devoted not merely to confronting the world's most pressing problems, but to building a better future for generations to come.

A NEW MESSAGE TO THE WORLD

The evening's final presentation turned from the extraordinary achievements of the past to the possibilities of the future.

Mr. Miscavige unveiled "Change," a new worldwide campaign introducing Scientology as the Technology of Change.

At its heart was a universal aspiration: the ability to change something in ourselves, our lives or the world around us. With a message transcending borders, languages and cultures, the campaign invites people everywhere to discover the practical tools of Scientology and the possibilities they offer.

And it all comes down to one simple, personal question:

"What do you want to change?"

As the evening drew to its close, Mr. Miscavige brought the celebration full circle, returning to the very thought with which it began: that history belongs to those who determine what tomorrow will be.

But now, after a night of historic victories and lives transformed, he carried that thought one step further.

"The true measure of what we do is not simply what we have changed," he declared. "It is what we have made possible."

And as the Grand Marquee rose in a final thunderous ovation, the 42nd IAS Anniversary drew to a triumphant close—a celebration of history already made, and a resounding declaration that the greatest chapters are yet to be written.

A WEEKEND OF CELEBRATION AT SAINT HILL

And the celebration was far from over.

Saturday brought the IAS Global Salvage Seminar, where members gathered to learn how to carry the momentum of the Anniversary into action, with plans for expanding IAS-sponsored humanitarian campaigns in communities around the world.

By Saturday evening, the Grand Marquee had undergone a spectacular transformation. Where thousands had risen in celebration the night before, an elegant ballroom now welcomed guests for the annual IAS Patrons Ball, honoring those whose exceptional generosity and commitment sustain the association's worldwide humanitarian work. The black-tie gala featured performances by Grammy Award-winning composer and musician Mark Isham and legendary drummer Woody Woodmansey.

On Sunday, the festivities continued with the annual Saint Hill Charity Concert, carrying forward a tradition established by L. Ron Hubbard himself: bringing the community together in support of local charities whose work enriches lives throughout the region.

From the triumphs celebrated on Friday night to the commitments renewed throughout the weekend, the 42nd IAS Anniversary stood as a testament to a movement united in purpose—and determined to shape the future.

Formed in 1984, the International Association of Scientologists (IAS) is the official membership organization of Scientology. Open to Scientologists of every nation, the IAS exists to unite, advance, support and protect the Scientology religion and Scientologists throughout the world so as to achieve the Aims of Scientology as originated by L. Ron Hubbard: "A civilization without insanity, without criminals and without war, where the able can prosper and honest beings can have rights, and where Man is free to rise to greater heights."

data.title: CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE UNVEILS THE NEXT WAVE OF VACATIONS FROM SEA TO SHORE, INCLUDING A NEW SHIP CLASS AND EXPANSION OF CELEBRATION KEY
data.description:
CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE UNVEILS THE NEXT WAVE OF VACATIONS FROM SEA TO SHORE, INCLUDING A NEW SHIP CLASS AND EXPANSION OF CELEBRATION KEY

CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE UNVEILS THE NEXT WAVE OF VACATIONS FROM SEA TO SHORE, INCLUDING A NEW SHIP CLASS AND EXPANSION OF CELEBRATION KEY

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026

New Ships, Expanded Destinations and Enhanced Guest Experiences Shape Carnival's Next Chapter

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Carnival Cruise Line President Christine Duffy today announced plans for two new ships that will introduce a new class to the Carnival fleet. To be built by long-time partner Fincantieri and delivered in 2033 and 2035, the approximately 130,000-gross-ton LNG-powered ships are intentionally designed on a smaller scale, enabling access to more ports and expanding destination and itinerary choices.

"With a 29-ship fleet, we know our guests appreciate choices," said Duffy. "They love the incredible experiences and amenities on our Excel Class ships, the largest in our fleet, but they also love the intimacy our smaller ships offer. This new class gives us the best of both worlds, helping future-proof our fleet with the flexibility to take America's Cruise Line to even more places in the years ahead."

Duffy also shared a first look at Carnival Destiny, major expansions at Celebration Key, Grand Bahama, enhancements at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay and plans to extend popular onboard benefits ashore. With more than 6.5 million guests sailing each year, Carnival has a unique perspective on what guests want from their vacations and is putting that feedback at the center of what comes next.

"Guests are seeking more choice, more flexibility and more ways to make the most of their time together," said Duffy. "What we are announcing today reflects how we're making Carnival cruise vacations even more personal, connected and fun."

Carnival Destiny Delivers More Choice with More Sea to See

Carnival Destiny, debuting in 2029 and the first of three Ace Class ships, is designed to give guests more ways to shape their cruise vacation around what they enjoy most. Built around its promise of More Sea to See, the ship will bring guests closer to the ocean with more outdoor space, expansive views and venues that make the sea part of the experience. Highlights include:

  • More outdoor pools than any other Carnival ship, including the first outward-facing main pool zone. Throughout the ship there will be eight pools, including six infinity pools, totaling more than 11,200 square feet of water surface,

  • An expansive ocean-front lanai that features several pools and brings dining and bar venues closer to the sea,

  • New premium venues with sweeping multideck ocean views, including a new exclusive pool on Deck 18 Aft, a total of 25 new dining and bar experiences, as well as a reimagined Limelight Lounge.

Carnival Destiny will dedicate nearly twice the space to family venues and attractions compared with Carnival's newest ships, bringing a family zone with mini golf, arcades, dining and other family favorites together in one area. It will also introduce Dr. Seuss Splash Station, a new splash pad inspired by The Cat in the Hat and Thing One and Thing Two, featuring water cannons and a dedicated area for children in swim diapers. The new attraction builds on Carnival's 13-year partnership with Dr. Seuss Enterprises and expands its popular Seuss at Sea programming.

Adults will have more choices of their own, with Carnival Destiny introducing Carnival's first adult-only zone spanning four decks. The zone will feature Carnival's first adult-only staterooms, an expanded Serenity adult-only retreat and an exclusive rooftop pool deck.

More Choice Ashore: The Next Evolution of Paradise Collection

Duffy also shared that Carnival is expanding the choices available ashore with the next evolution of Paradise Collection by Carnival, the largest portfolio of exclusive destinations across The Bahamas, Caribbean and Mexico.

The collection includes six distinct destinations: Celebration Key in Grand Bahama; RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay; Isla Tropicale in Roatan; Amber Cove in the Dominican Republic; Puerta Maya in Cozumel and Grand Turk in Turks & Caicos.

Building on the early success of Celebration Key, which has welcomed more than 3.25 million guests since its opening in July 2025, Carnival revealed plans for two new expansion phases for the destination that will increase total land-side capacity by 6,000 guests, with 3,000 added in each phase.

In 2028, a new portal will introduce even more ways for guests to play and relax together with a heated, beach-entry pool with a swim-up bar; a new social waterslide designed for four to five guests to slide together; and a colorful, aqua play area featuring five waterslides, a dry climbing play structure and drenching bucket created especially for younger children.

In 2030, a new major water park will add 18 waterslides, the cruise industry's longest lazy river with float-up bars and swim-in/swim-out cabanas, as well as a new exclusive area with an infinity pool, more beach access and new dining and bar concepts.

Carnival also announced Serenity Beach, a new complimentary retreat for guests 21 and older coming to RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay in spring 2027. It will feature dedicated loungers and bar and beverage service, with daybeds and cabanas available for an additional charge.

Greater Value from Ship to Shore

Beginning in February 2027, Carnival will extend its drink packages CHEERS!, CHEERS! Zero Proof™, Bottomless Bubbles™ and CHEERS! Social to Celebration Key and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, giving guests who purchase these Carnival packages greater value for their vacation dollars.

For additional information on Carnival Cruise Line and to book a cruise vacation on Carnival, call 1-800-CARNIVAL, visit http://carnival.com or contact your favorite travel advisor or online travel site.

ABOUT CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE

Carnival Cruise Line, part of Carnival Corporation (NYSE: CCL), the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide – and is proud to be known as America's Cruise Line and for carrying more Americans and serving more U.S. homeports than any other. Carnival sails more than six and a half million guests annually and in 2023 was the first cruise line to sail more than 100 million guests in total. Operating from 13 U.S. and four Australian homeports, as well as seasonally from Europe, Carnival hosts more than 95,000 guests on its ships every day of the year and employs more than 50,000 team members, representing 120 nationalities.

Since its founding in 1972, Carnival has continually revolutionized the cruise industry and popularized the cruise vacation as an affordable and fun travel option. Carnival's fleet of 29 ships reflects an exciting period of growth that continues with the addition of seven ships through 2035: a fourth and fifth Excel class ship scheduled for 2027 and 2028, respectively; three Ace class ships scheduled for delivery in 2029, 2031 and 2033, beginning with Carnival Destiny; and two additional ships in the new class expected to be delivered in 2033 and 2035. Carnival's newest guest offering is its all-new exclusive destination, Celebration Key on Grand Bahama, which debuted in 2025 to join the company's Paradise Collection of Caribbean gems.
